title: return vs no return
idea: TOOL: a sub-plan with no return hands back nothing useful; return is what gives a usable value.

exercises.prompt:
def show(n):
    print(n)

x = show(5)

This prints 5. But what is stored in x?
options: None (nothing useful) - show has no return
exercises.explanation: show only prints; it never returns a value. So x gets None - there was nothing handed back to store.

exercises.prompt: A sub-plan that only prints does NOT hand back a usable value.
exercises.explanation: Right. Printing shows something on screen but returns nothing. To get a value back you must use return.

exercises.prompt:
def give(n):
    return n

x = give(5)

What is x now?
options: Nothing prints and x is empty
exercises.explanation: give uses return, so give(5) hands back 5 and x becomes 5. return is what makes a value usable.

exercises.prompt: You want 'y = f(3)' to store a real number in y. What must f do?
options: Use return to hand a value back
exercises.explanation: To store a value from a call, the sub-plan must return it. A print alone leaves y holding None.

exercises.explanation: add computes sum_result but never returns it, so the call hands back None. The computed value is lost.

exercises.prompt: Match each sub-plan body to what its call hands back.
exercises.explanation: Only return hands a usable value back. Printing or computing without returning both give None to the caller.

exercises.prompt: Fix the broken sub-plan. Order lines so add(a,b) RETURNS the sum.
exercises.explanation: Add the missing return. Now the computed total is handed back instead of being thrown away.

exercises.prompt:
def f(n):
    return n

print(f(7))

What prints?
exercises.explanation: f returns 7, so print(f(7)) prints 7. The returned value flows straight into print.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: both print and return 'end' something. What does return specifically give you that print does not?
options: A value the caller can store and reuse
exercises.explanation: print shows; return gives back. Only return produces a value the rest of your program can keep using.

exercises.prompt: If you forget the return, your sub-plan may still run - but the caller gets None instead of the answer.
exercises.explanation: Yes. A missing return is a common bug: the work happens but the result is never handed back.
